name: write_two_results_to_record
description: Calls two other routines, then writes two byte-sized results into fixed offsets of a record passed in through an address register. The inputs come from registers the decompiler could not name, so the exact values are not certain.

name: merge_byte_into_four_buffers
description: Walks eight rows of four buffers spaced a fixed distance apart, updating each from the source byte under one bit of a control value. The sign of the input selects one of two variants, and the non-negative variant first calls one routine and uses its result.

name: emit_signed_decimal_digits
description: Takes a signed 16-bit value, works on its magnitude, and sends its five decimal digits, most significant first, to an output routine as character codes. A final call follows the digits.

name: call_routine_four_times_then_once
description: Calls one routine four times in a counted loop, then calls a second routine once. It does no work of its own beyond this sequence.

name: forward_to_constant_merge
description: Does no work of its own beyond calling a one-instruction helper that merges a fixed constant into a data register, then returning. Two routines call it.

name: toggle_high_bits_of_word
description: Toggles the two highest bits of a shared 16-bit variable and returns. It does nothing else.

name: initialise_pointer_table_and_state
description: Calls one routine, then fills a table of pointers computed from offsets in a data block until a terminator value. It then clears several state variables, copies a list of entries up to a negative value, and sets an enable flag.

name: advance_sample_playback_tick
description: Does nothing while the playback flag is clear. Otherwise it counts ticks and, at a set period, advances a position through a table of segments, updates per-channel values for channels whose flags are set, and clears the playback flag at the end of the last segment unless a repeat flag is set; on other ticks it calls a helper for each channel whose byte is non-zero.

name: stop_playback_and_clear_state
description: Clears the playback flag and four related state variables, the same reset the playback tick performs when a sequence ends. Three routines call it.

name: apply_channel_slide_effect
description: Runs one effect step for a channel, calling one of two helpers first when an enable word is set. Effect codes 1, 6, 7 and 8 lower a stored value by a parameter down to a floor, codes 2, 9, 10 and 11 raise it up to a ceiling, and code 13 adjusts a level kept between zero and 64; codes 0, 3, 4 and 5 look up a word in a table and write it to the output block.

name: add_capped_level_delta
description: Adds the incoming 16-bit delta to a stored level, caps the result at 64, and writes it to the output block.

name: subtract_masked_level_floor_zero
description: Subtracts an input value with bits 4 to 7 cleared from a stored 16-bit level, floors the result at zero, and writes it to the output block.

name: advance_sequence_position_counter
description: Computes a new position from the input byte, shifted left by seven and increased by sixteen, and stores it. When the position reaches 1024 it wraps to zero and increments a segment counter; when that counter reaches the stored segment count and a flag is zero, it clears the playback flag and four state variables.

name: parse_channel_event_record
description: Reads an event record for one audio channel and updates the channel's stored pointer, period and length from it, using a table indexed by the high nibble of the record's second byte. It then applies the effect code: one code stores a whole value directly, one sets a level from the record's third byte, and one acts only when the low nibble of that byte is set.

name: check_key_then_open_intuition
description: Compares a stored key byte with the code for the character nine, with its top bit clear. On a match it opens intuition.library through the exec library and then loops endlessly on a library call; otherwise it returns.

name: stub_one_call_unknown_body
description: Decompilation of this routine did not complete, so its body is unknown. The only established facts are about 30 instructions and one call to an unnamed routine, and its purpose cannot be determined from this evidence.

name: poll_jump_entry_until_zero
description: Repeatedly calls a jump-table entry that forwards to a fixed address, and keeps calling while the value it returns is non-zero. It returns once that value is zero.

name: access_audio_dma_registers
description: Decompilation of this routine did not complete, so only its structure is known: about 44 instructions, one call to an unnamed routine, and access to the four audio channel pointer and length registers and the DMA control register. Nothing beyond these facts is established.

name: copy_record_word_to_output
description: Copies a 16-bit field from the input record into a fixed field of the output block and returns. Nothing else is done.

name: store_nonzero_low_nibble
description: Reads a 16-bit field of the input record. When its low nibble is non-zero it clears a long field of the state block and stores the nibble in another field; otherwise it does nothing.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decoded instructions are not valid code: after storing one constant address the bytes decode as bad data. The routine therefore has no usable behaviour.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Contains only a return, so it performs no work.
